[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Hugh was born about 1700 and is recognized as the son of [[Glasgow-1057|John Glasgow]]. 

=== Family Connection ===
Information provided by Elaine suggests that William Glasgow had a brother named [[Glasgow-1056|Hugh]], who married [[Kilpatrick-1635|Janet (Kilpatrick) Glasgow]]. They were sons of [[Glasgow-1057|John Glasgow (abt.1644-abt.1700)]] and [[Spark-330|Agnes (Spark) Glasgow]].<ref>https://archive.is/9OGiC</ref>

=== Distinguishing Different Individuals ===
It's important to distinguish this Hugh from other individuals with the same name:
* [[Glasgow-1067|Hew Glasgow (1676-)]]
* [[Glasgow-1706|Hew Glasgow (1706-)]]
* [[Glasgow-1603|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1600-)]]

=== Children of Hugh Glasgow ===
Hugh Glasgow’s children are recorded in the Ayr Extract 1981 & 1988 IGI records, which include:
* Glasgow, Thomas (M) - Christened 7 Nov 1725, Ayr, Kilwinning
* Glasgow, Janet (F) - Christened 15 Feb 1713, Ayr, Kilwinning
* Glasgow, William (M) - Christened 26 Jun 1715, Ayr, Kilwinning
* Glasgow, John (M) - Christened 2 Jul 1721, Ayr, Kilwinning
* Glasgow, Margaret (F) - Christened 17 Mar 1723, Ayr, Kilwinning
* Glasgow, Agnes (F) - Christened 18 Dec 1726, Ayr, Kilwinning

== Research Notes ==
=== Kilwinning family reassessment, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing Hugh [[Glasgow-1056]] → father John [[Glasgow-1057]] relationship is now probable, 74%, superseding the earlier 58% possible assessment. The family account attributed to Elaine Comes identifies Hugh, husband of Janet Kilpatrick, as William Glasgow’s brother and names their parents John Glasgow and Agnes Spark. William’s held Stevenston child citation names that same parental couple, also recorded with George at Kilwinning in 1687. Hugh’s Kilwinning family from 1710 belongs to the same local generation. These specific people, spouse and household make John-1057 the probable father. The incorrect Glasgow-1080 hyperlink in John’s duplicate quotation is an editorial inconsistency: Hugh’s own captured account links John-1057 correctly and both texts name John and Agnes Spark. It is not evidence for a competing parent. The household records corroborate the named couple, while Hugh’s siblinghood and transfer of that fatherhood still depend on the single secondary account; duplicated quotations are not independent testimony.

74% assesses the complete Hugh-to-John/Agnes-household father identification, from 58% possible. The sibling relationship is reported, not independently proved. No Hugh childhood record or underlying evidence for Elaine’s statement was inspected. John’s own 1661 Edinburgh-child identification, the unrelated 1685 testament comparison, other ancestry and all mothers retain separate assessments. The circa-1692/1700 estimates are not birth records; no dates are changed.

Next useful evidence: Find the underlying evidence for Elaine’s specific brother/parent statement, or an identifying marriage, apprenticeship or inheritance record for Hugh. Rechecking the broken hyperlink alone cannot resolve the historical relationship.

=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1057]] is assessed at 58% (possible). The held Elaine Comes family account specifically describes Hugh, husband of Janet Kilpatrick, and brother William as sons of John and Agnes Spark. Hugh’s adult family is established by the repeated Kilwinning parent pair, and c1692 fits John’s generation. This is a specific secondary family attribution rather than surname alone. However no Hugh childhood record is held, and the quotation’s John-1080 link actually points to Jonat, a female1615 child; that unresolved error prevents probable confidence.

Complete inherited Hugh-to-John placement58%, possible. John/Agnes adult identity and John’s proposed Edinburgh childhood are separate. Descendant baptisms do not identify Hugh’s own father.

Next useful test: Resolve the secondary account’s wrong1080 link and identify its underlying family source or Hugh’s own parent record.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.is/9OGiC https://archive.is/9OGiC]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.
